bull_bear.body:
- Preferred manufacturer and supplier position in the Power sector for Lube Oil Systems, with a customer base of reputed domestic customers and leading MNCs
- Leading and established supplier position in the machine tool sector for Industrial Lubrication Systems, particularly CNC
- Ability to offer customised, application-specific systems built to international certifications (CE / UL), enabling access to European and US customers
- Two manufacturing locations (Faridabad and Bengaluru) supporting a diversified industrial customer base
- Entry into the 800 MW Oil Consoles business adds a high-barrier product to the portfolio for large-capacity power projects
- Strong on-delivery performance and reduced project execution time cited as reinforcing customer confidence
- ERP system implemented, improving internal financial controls, inventory management and supply chain
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Raw material and input price volatility with inflationary pressure — Management flags inflationary pressures and fluctuations in the prices of raw materials and other inputs as areas requiring continuous attention; as a build-to-order engineering manufacturer, input cost moves on fixed-price project contracts compress margins. Mitigation cited is better planning, lean manufacturing, inventory optimisation and vendor development.
- Rising manpower cost and availability of skilled personnel — Increasing cost of manpower and availability of skilled personnel are explicitly flagged as continuing concerns. The business depends on technical and project-management capability, so the Company is countering with skill development, employee engagement and retention of trained manpower.
- Competitive pressure on pricing and profitability — Competition in both domestic and international markets is stated to exert pressure on pricing and profitability; increasing competition is also listed among the factors the business is subject to. Management's response is product development, customisation, quality improvement and cost optimisation.
- Dependence on customer project investment cycles and Government policy — Business in the Company's sectors is stated to be subject to Government policies and project investment cycles. Demand is capital-expenditure-led — power, oil & gas, steel, cement and infrastructure projects — so a pause in customer capex directly defers order inflow.
- Geopolitical developments and changes in global trade conditions affecting exports — Management states that international geopolitical developments and changes in global trade conditions may affect export opportunities and project execution. The Company serves international customers and supplies CE / UL compliant systems to European and US markets, so trade conditions bear directly on that revenue.
- Project execution risk — Project execution is repeatedly identified as exposed — to international economic conditions, trade conditions and investment cycles. Close monitoring of project execution and reduced execution time are cited as mitigations, indicating execution is managed as a live risk rather than a settled process.
- International economic conditions — Listed by management among the various factors to which business in the Company's sectors is subject, alongside Government policies and project investment cycles.
- Reliance on internal control and ERP systems for financial and operational integrity — The Company states it has a robust risk management framework and a Risk Management Policy, with an ERP system underpinning internal financial controls, inventory management and supply chain, and an Internal Auditor reporting quarterly to the Audit Committee — making the adequacy of these systems a structural dependency.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Cenlub Industries designs and manufactures Lube Oil Systems, Industrial Lubrication Systems and associated fluid-handling equipment for industrial customers. It supplies the power generation sector (lube oil systems and oil consoles), the oil & gas sector (customised, application-specific lubrication and fluid handling systems built to CE / UL requirements) and the machine tool sector, where it serves steel, cement, sugar, paper and CNC machine-tool customers. Its customer base spans reputed domestic customers, leading MNCs and international markets, and during FY26 it developed a new range of lubrication systems for the construction sector and Heavy Earth Moving Machinery.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Power:** Lube Oil Systems and associated equipment, Oil Consoles (incl. 800 MW Oil Consoles)
- **Oil & Gas:** Customised lubrication systems, Fluid handling systems (CE / UL compliant)
- **Machine Tools / Industrial:** Industrial Lubrication Systems
- **Construction & Heavy Earth Moving Machinery:** New range of lubrication systems for construction sector and Heavy Earth Moving Machinery

business.body:
- Preferred manufacturer and supplier position in the Power sector for Lube Oil Systems, with a customer base of reputed domestic customers and leading MNCs
- Leading and established supplier position in the machine tool sector for Industrial Lubrication Systems, particularly CNC
- Ability to offer customised, application-specific systems built to international certifications (CE / UL), enabling access to European and US customers
- Two manufacturing locations (Faridabad and Bengaluru) supporting a diversified industrial customer base
- Entry into the 800 MW Oil Consoles business adds a high-barrier product to the portfolio for large-capacity power projects
- Strong on-delivery performance and reduced project execution time cited as reinforcing customer confidence
- ERP system implemented, improving internal financial controls, inventory management and supply chain
business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Strengthen existing customer relationships while developing new products and applications and expanding presence in emerging business segments
- Consolidate the preferred-supplier position in the Power sector for Lube Oil Systems and scale the newly entered 800 MW Oil Consoles business in India and international markets
- Grow the Oil & Gas vertical with customised, application-specific lubrication and fluid handling systems built to CE / UL requirements for European and US markets
- Defend the leading position in industrial lubrication for machine tools (particularly CNC) and the steel, cement, sugar and paper industries from the Faridabad and Bengaluru facilities
- Diversify the core lubrication business into the construction sector and Heavy Earth Moving Machinery, opening construction, mining and heavy-equipment opportunities
- Continue investing in product development, manufacturing infrastructure and process improvement to build capability for future growth
- Improve manufacturing efficiency, reduce project execution time and maintain on-delivery performance
- Strengthen capabilities in customised systems and international certifications to serve global customers
- Repay debt with the intent of becoming debt free
- Pursue energy efficiency, including evaluating installation of a solar power plant at the manufacturing facility to raise the renewable share of the energy mix
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company discloses no named expansion project, capacity addition or capex quantum. The narrative describes continuing, unquantified investment: it "continues to invest in product development, manufacturing infrastructure and process improvement" to increase capabilities and prepare for future growth, and has "made appropriate investments in plant, machinery and facilities" relating to statutory requirements, environmental protection, pollution control and sustainability. Capability expansion in FY26 was product-led rather than brick-and-mortar: entry into the 800 MW Oil Consoles business for large-capacity power projects and development of a new range of lubrication systems for the construction sector and Heavy Earth Moving Machinery, served from the existing Faridabad and Bengaluru manufacturing facilities. On the energy side the Faridabad facility uses PNG gensets during electricity outages, older low-efficiency motors, heaters and fans are being progressively replaced with higher-efficiency alternatives, and the Company is evaluating the installation of a solar power plant at its manufacturing facility to raise the renewable share of its energy mix; no size, cost or commissioning date is stated for that solar plant.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Encouraging demand continued from various domestic industrial sectors as well as international markets despite a challenging external environment
- Entry into the 800 MW Oil Consoles business is expected to create opportunities in the large-capacity power project segment in India and internationally
- Power, construction, mining and infrastructure sectors are stated to provide significant potential for the Company's lubrication systems
- The Oil & Gas sector, both domestic and international, continues to offer encouraging opportunities
- New product lines provide an opportunity to enter a large and growing application segment, with the outlook described as very positive
- Management expects improved business performance in coming years through focused product development, enhanced operational efficiency, improved customer service and expansion into new market segments
- Customer-relationship strengthening, new product/application development and expansion into emerging segments are expected to provide a stronger foundation for growth in the coming years
- Demand is exposed to Government policies, project investment cycles, international economic conditions and increasing competition
- During FY26 the Company secured orders for Oil Consoles for 800 MW power projects, marking its entry into the 800 MW Oil Consoles business (no order-book value or quantum disclosed)
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

risks.risk: Raw material and input price volatility with inflationary pressure
risks.note: Management flags inflationary pressures and fluctuations in the prices of raw materials and other inputs as areas requiring continuous attention; as a build-to-order engineering manufacturer, input cost moves on fixed-price project contracts compress margins. Mitigation cited is better planning, lean manufacturing, inventory optimisation and vendor development.

risks.risk: Rising manpower cost and availability of skilled personnel
risks.note: Increasing cost of manpower and availability of skilled personnel are explicitly flagged as continuing concerns. The business depends on technical and project-management capability, so the Company is countering with skill development, employee engagement and retention of trained manpower.

risks.risk: Competitive pressure on pricing and profitability
risks.note: Competition in both domestic and international markets is stated to exert pressure on pricing and profitability; increasing competition is also listed among the factors the business is subject to. Management's response is product development, customisation, quality improvement and cost optimisation.

risks.risk: Dependence on customer project investment cycles and Government policy
risks.note: Business in the Company's sectors is stated to be subject to Government policies and project investment cycles. Demand is capital-expenditure-led — power, oil & gas, steel, cement and infrastructure projects — so a pause in customer capex directly defers order inflow.

risks.risk: Geopolitical developments and changes in global trade conditions affecting exports
risks.note: Management states that international geopolitical developments and changes in global trade conditions may affect export opportunities and project execution. The Company serves international customers and supplies CE / UL compliant systems to European and US markets, so trade conditions bear directly on that revenue.

Project execution is repeatedly identified as exposed — to international economic conditions, trade conditions and investment cycles. Close monitoring of project execution and reduced execution time are cited as mitigations, indicating execution is managed as a live risk rather than a settled process.
Listed by management among the various factors to which business in the Company's sectors is subject, alongside Government policies and project investment cycles.

risks.risk: Reliance on internal control and ERP systems for financial and operational integrity
risks.note: The Company states it has a robust risk management framework and a Risk Management Policy, with an ERP system underpinning internal financial controls, inventory management and supply chain, and an Internal Auditor reporting quarterly to the Audit Committee — making the adequacy of these systems a structural dependency.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Cenlub Industries is a Faridabad-based manufacturer of industrial lubrication systems, lube oil systems and fluid handling equipment, and during FY26 entered the 800 MW Oil Consoles business for large-capacity power projects.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Cenlub Industries designs and manufactures Lube Oil Systems, Industrial Lubrication Systems and associated fluid-handling equipment for industrial customers. It supplies the power generation sector (lube oil systems and oil consoles), the oil & gas sector (customised, application-specific lubrication and fluid handling systems built to CE / UL requirements) and the machine tool sector, where it serves steel, cement, sugar, paper and CNC machine-tool customers. Its customer base spans reputed domestic customers, leading MNCs and international markets, and during FY26 it developed a new range of lubrication systems for the construction sector and Heavy Earth Moving Machinery.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body: - Bharthari Securities Limited — related party: Other listed company in which Mr. Dinesh Kaushal, Non-Executive Independent Director of Cenlub, holds a directorship as Non-Executive Independent Director — a directorship interest only, not a subsidiary, JV or associate of Cenlub

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Power:** Lube Oil Systems and associated equipment, Oil Consoles (incl. 800 MW Oil Consoles)
- **Oil & Gas:** Customised lubrication systems, Fluid handling systems (CE / UL compliant)
- **Machine Tools / Industrial:** Industrial Lubrication Systems
- **Construction & Heavy Earth Moving Machinery:** New range of lubrication systems for construction sector and Heavy Earth Moving Machinery

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Power generation (including large-capacity 800 MW power projects)
- Oil & Gas (domestic and international)
- Machine tools, particularly the CNC segment
- Steel
- Cement
- Sugar
- Paper
- Construction, mining and heavy equipment
- India (domestic industrial sectors)
- Europe and the US (CE / UL compliant systems)

certifications.title: Certs (RHP)
certifications.body: CE / UL compliance for lubrication and fluid handling systems supplied to European and US markets

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Encouraging demand continued from various domestic industrial sectors as well as international markets despite a challenging external environment
- Entry into the 800 MW Oil Consoles business is expected to create opportunities in the large-capacity power project segment in India and internationally
- Power, construction, mining and infrastructure sectors are stated to provide significant potential for the Company's lubrication systems
- The Oil & Gas sector, both domestic and international, continues to offer encouraging opportunities
- New product lines provide an opportunity to enter a large and growing application segment, with the outlook described as very positive
- Management expects improved business performance in coming years through focused product development, enhanced operational efficiency, improved customer service and expansion into new market segments
- Customer-relationship strengthening, new product/application development and expansion into emerging segments are expected to provide a stronger foundation for growth in the coming years
- Demand is exposed to Government policies, project investment cycles, international economic conditions and increasing competition
- During FY26 the Company secured orders for Oil Consoles for 800 MW power projects, marking its entry into the 800 MW Oil Consoles business (no order-book value or quantum disclosed)

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Strengthen existing customer relationships while developing new products and applications and expanding presence in emerging business segments
- Consolidate the preferred-supplier position in the Power sector for Lube Oil Systems and scale the newly entered 800 MW Oil Consoles business in India and international markets
- Grow the Oil & Gas vertical with customised, application-specific lubrication and fluid handling systems built to CE / UL requirements for European and US markets
- Defend the leading position in industrial lubrication for machine tools (particularly CNC) and the steel, cement, sugar and paper industries from the Faridabad and Bengaluru facilities
- Diversify the core lubrication business into the construction sector and Heavy Earth Moving Machinery, opening construction, mining and heavy-equipment opportunities
- Continue investing in product development, manufacturing infrastructure and process improvement to build capability for future growth
- Improve manufacturing efficiency, reduce project execution time and maintain on-delivery performance
- Strengthen capabilities in customised systems and international certifications to serve global customers
- Repay debt with the intent of becoming debt free
- Pursue energy efficiency, including evaluating installation of a solar power plant at the manufacturing facility to raise the renewable share of the energy mix
